articleTitle: Practical Application and Selection of Single-Phase to Three-Phase Converters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Rural Electric Power Conference
abstract: Three-phase motors and electronic power supplies are used in commercial and industrial equipment for economy and efficiency. When three-phase power is not available from the utility, another source must be provided. Gasoline or diesel generators may be used, or the available single-phase utility power may be converted to three-phase power. This paper examines the technologies available and offers specific recommendations for the selection of converters for specific applications.

articleTitle: Practical High Impedance Fault Detection for Distribution Feeders
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Rural Electric Power Conference
abstract: Distribution protection systems must balance dependability with security considerations to be practical. This is quite difficult for high impedance faults. Only highly sensitive algorithms can achieve absolute dependability in detecting very low current faults. This high sensitivity results in a propensity for false tripping, creating a less secure system and resulting in the potential for decreased service continuity and lower reliability. Researchers at Texas A&M University have balanced fault detection with fault discrimination, resulting in a practical combination of detection algorithms in a commercially viable system. This device has many "intelligent" features, including the ability to analyze and correlate numerous fault characteristics in real time so that it can make a correct determination of the status of the feeder with a high degree of accuracy. This paper describes this system, which uses multiple algorithms to detect various types of faults and an expert decision maker to decipher incoming data to determine the status and health of a distribution feeder. Requirements for a practical, secure high impedance fault relay are also discussed. Finally, Texas A&M has licensed this technology to a commercial partner, which manufactures a device that detects high impedance faults in addition to performing numerous other monitoring and protection functions.

articleTitle: Vegetation Management on Distribution Line Right-of-Way Are You Getting Top Value for Your Money?
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Rural Electric Power Conference
abstract: In regions of the country where rainfall and sunlight combine to produce vigorous plant growth, the electric utility's right-of-way maintenance budget is usually second in size only to its wholesale power budget. A rural electric cooperative with 12,000 meters and 2,500 miles of distribution line may spend as much as $1,000,000 annually for clearing and trimming. Managers know that proper maintenance will: Improve service reliability, Reduce line loss, and Provide access to the distribution lines. Proof is easily obtained from outage reports and kilowatt hour usage accounts. The more difficult evaluation is to determine if top value is received for each right-of-way maintenance dollar spent, and if the existing program is the most efficient.

articleTitle: A Ouantum Leap Into The IED Age
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Rural Electric Power Conference
abstract: The integration of pattern recognition, artificial intelligence and advanced communication technologies in utility substation IED's (Intelligent Electronic Devices) has opened the door to practical and cost effective automation of power distribution systems. A major driver for the application of these new technologies has been the research directed toward the detection of high-impedance faults. The commercial products which embody these complex detection functions have already expanded to include most of the protection, control, and monitoring required at a utility substation. These new Super-IED's enable major utility initiatives, such as power quality management, improved public safety, operation and maintenance productivity, and power system automation.

articleTitle: Benefits to utilities from semiconducting linear low density polyethylene jackets on medium voltage
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Rural Electric Power Conference
abstract: Jackets are now recognized to provide cost effective cable protection in service and protect cables being direct buried or pulled into ducts. They very significantly retard damaging moisture penetration into the cable core. They also protect cable neutrals from physical damage and moisture corrosion. Semiconducting jackets combine these benefits and provide grounding approximating that of bare concentric neutrals. Linear low density polyethylene [LLDPE] insulating jacket and LLDPE semiconducting jacket have similar physical properties and provide almost equal physical protection to cables. Insulated cables are incrementally damaged by overvoltages from system and lightning surges. This electrical damage is minimized when correctly sized and installed arresters are used in conjunction with semiconducting LLDPE jacket or bare concentric neutrals.

articleTitle: Phase Frame Analysis of the Effects of Voltage Unbalance on Induction Machines
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Rural Electric Power Conference
abstract: Operating a three-phase induction motor with unbalanced voltages can lead to excessive heating.[l] The traditional method of analyzing the operating conditions of the motor when unbalanced voltages have been applied has been to use the theory of symmetrical components. The purpose of this paper is to develop a method of analyzing the motor in the “phase frame”. The method is then applied to a typical motor to demonstrate the results of operating a motor with unbalanced voltages and the reason why a motor must be derated under these conditions.

articleTitle: Establishing a lightning protection evaluation program for distribution and subtransmission lines
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Rural Electric Power Conference
abstract: The level of lightning protection on transmission, subtransmission, and distribution lines can be effectively evaluated with the use of historical outage information, lightning ground flash density data, information obtained on field inspections, and EPRI's Lightning Protection Design Workstation. Comparisons can be made between various methods of lightning protection for a given line to obtain the most beneficial and cost effective results.

articleTitle: THE IMPACT OF INSTALLING POWER FACTOR IMPROVEMENT CAPACITORS: AN OVERVIEW AND CASE STUDY
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Rural Electric Power Conference
abstract: This paper explores the installation of power factor improvement capacitors from the perspective of an existing electrical distribution system. The first portion of the paper provides an overview of power factor, including the advantages of power factor improvement. The second portion walks through a case study, outlining several electrical issues regarding the effects of capacitor operation with an existing distribution system, and recommending design considerations for a proper capacitor bank installation. NOTE: The views expressed in this paper do not necessarily represent the views of the United States of America or the U.S. General Services Administration.

articleTitle: Reducing Wholesale Power Costs on Rural Electric Coop Systems with Capacitors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Rural Electric Power Conference
abstract: Today, more than ever, Rural Electric Coop managers and engineers are looking for ways to reduce costs, and operate the distribution system as efficiently as possible. Wholesale power is the single largest expense incurred to operate the systems. It typidy represents 70 - 80% of an REC's total cost of operations System losses of 7 - 8% are common for cooperative distribution systems. These losses represent power that is lost in the system. They are the difference between power purchased and power sold. This represents a significant cost on an ongoing basis to maintain these losses. The application of capacitors to REC distribution systems has typically been carried out to maintain the power factor at the substation at a reasonable level. Cooperatives operating at average 90 - 92% power factor would typically not consider applying additional capacitors to the distribution system since this level of power factor achievement is considered “Good Enough” by many cooperatives. However, this paper will demonstrate that a significant reduction in operating costs can be achieved by reducing line losses with the proper selection and application of capacitor equipment. Additional systems benefits include improved voltage regulation, and reduced thermal demand on lines and equipment. This paper will describe the analysis performed on an actual cooperative 12.47 KV distribution substation serving four (4) rural feeders. System parameters, load data and cost data are placed in a computer program that models the system, performs an exhaustive load flow analysis on the model system, and produces an economic analysis that will allow an economic comparison between cases based on a number of different system configurations. This paper will demonstrate that it is practical and economically justifiable to apply capacitors on distribution systems which may be operating at 90 - 92% power factor. This paper will also demonstrate that power factor penalty clauses in some wholesale rates should not be the only motivation for capacitor implementation.

articleTitle: "WRITTEN-POLE" MOTOR-GENERATOR WITH INTEGRAL ENGINE PROVIDES NO-BATTERY UPS
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Rural Electric Power Conference
abstract: A "written-poie"TM motor drives a "written-pole" generator. The M-G set continuously provides power isolation between utility power and sensitive loads. Inertial "flywheel" energy in the rotating M-G set provides 15 seconds of full load ride-through during momentary power interruptions, while the written-pole technology maintains precise frequency and voltage to the load. The M-G set easily reaccelerates to full synchronous speed when utility power is restored. For longer blackouts, an internal combustion engine, integrated in the package design, starts after about 10 seconds and operates the M-G to provide uninterruptible power as long as fuel is supplied.

articleTitle: PREDESIGNED STEEL POLE USE ON 69 KV LINES WITH DISTRIBUTION UNDERBUILD
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Rural Electric Power Conference
abstract: Central lowa Power Cooperative (ClPCO) is a generation and transmission cooperative serving fourteen distribution cooperatives in central lowa. CPCO systematically rebuilds its backbone 34.5 kV transmission system. The current regu!atoty and right-of-way environment is resulting in decisions to utilize public rights-of-way for line routings. At the same time, county and state transportation departments are increasing& restricting the use of public right-of-way in order to create clear zones of minimal roadside obstructions. This creates limitations on the traditional use of guyed poles. Anchoring easements are also becoming increasingly difficult to obtain from private property owners in rural areas because of the negative effects on farming operations. All these factors create the need for cost-effective, unguyed structures.

articleTitle: LONGITUDINALLY CORRUGATED TAPE SHIELDED MEDIUM VOLTAGE UNDERGROUND CABLES
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Rural Electric Power Conference
abstract: Longitudinally corrugated copper tape shielded medium voltage underground cable is a construction primarily used on main feeders of a utility's underground distribution system The benefits include higher short circuit current, higher conductor ampacity, lower PR losses, and improved cable performance by slowing water migration.

articleTitle: ELECTRICAL FIELD MEASUREMENTS ON AN EPRI 2 POLE, 20 HP WRITTEN POLE MOTOR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Rural Electric Power Conference
abstract: The recent introduction of the EPRI single phase Written Pole soft-start motor may open new possibilities and marketing opportunities for rural electric cooperatives The new single phase high efficiency AC motor technology promises softstart capabilities that allow designs and application of up to 60 HP, 240 volt motors. This paper will summarize some of the technical aspects of the new single phase motor technology. An actual field test and application of a Written Pole motor will also be used to compare motor starting currents and line flicker with manufacturer’s literature and specifications.

articleTitle: Load management using pole mounted RTUs
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Rural Electric Power Conference
abstract: This paper reviews the practical aspects of using pole mounted RTUs to trim peak kW demand at smaller electric utilities. Two case studies are presented which show varying methods of lowering demand charges. Financial issues of cost-justifying the acquisition of a peak-shaving system and post audit is also discussed. Although other types of RTUs exist, such as card cage and free standing rack mounted types, the RTUs mentioned here are restricted to small, transducerless, pole mounted RTUs.

articleTitle: RAPTOR ELECTROCUTIONS ON ELECTRIC UTILITY DISTRIBUTION OVERHEAD STRUCTURES
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Rural Electric Power Conference
abstract: Distribution powerline raptor electrocutions have been studied extensively since 1971. Numerous methods to modify powerline structures to eliminate the potential for electrocutions have been developed, published, and utilized by the electric utility industry. Some of the modified overhead distribution line construction units have been adopted as standards by investor owned utilities and the Rural Utilities Service, dramatically reducing raptor electrocutions. Although utility construction practices have improved greatly since 1971, some raptor electrocutions still persist. Many utilities today are employing larger crossarms in their new construction to provide increased phase-to-phase and phase-to-ground separation to reduce the potential for electrocutions. Although an emphasis on providing increased phase separation may eliminate some electrocutions, uninsulated jumper wires may pose a greater threat to raptors. A review of utility raptor electrocution forms filed with the Rural Utilities Service since 1985 indicates that overhead distribution powerline poles configured with transformers and bare jumpers are associated with the most raptor electrocutions.

articleTitle: Application of Padmounted Fault Interrupters to Single-Phase URD Systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Rural Electric Power Conference
abstract: A distribution planner once remarked that if five designers were given the same task of laying out a residential underground distribution system that between them they would produce ten different designs. This is perhaps an exaggeration, but it is certainly true that each designer seeks to optimize their design decisions taking into account the various present and future factors of cost, operation, maintenance, system growth and the interests of both the utility and the consumer in quality of service, system reliability, safety, and aesthetics.

articleTitle: Using distribution static compensators (D-STATCOMs) to extend the capability of voltage-limited distribution feeders
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Rural Electric Power Conference
abstract: The application of distribution system static synchronous compensators (D-STATCOMs) are examined for distribution voltage regulation. In particular, the concern of voltage regulation on long, voltage-limited feeders is considered and the D-STATCOM is shown to be a cost-effective means of resolving it.

articleTitle: Forty Years of the IEEE Rural Electric Power Committee 1955-1995
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Rural Electric Power Conference
abstract: As in many other organizations, the IEEE IAS Rural Electric Power Committee has operated under different titles and society structures. The first title was the Farm Electrification Subcommittee which was formed in 1953 under the Domestic and Commercial Applications Committee of the American Institute of Electrical Engineers (AIEE). The history and work of the committee are outlined covering 1955-1995.
